supportTargets.tools: Repository automation may inspect governed files but must not become a product runtime dependency.
supportTargets.planning: Planning state may drive automation but product runtime code must not read or mutate the backlog.
supportTargets.docs: Documentation is authority and guidance, not a runtime configuration source unless a task defines a generated contract.
supportTargets.design: Approved experience references drive generation and conformance; they are not shipped as mutable application state.
supportTargets.evaluation: Versioned benchmark and golden-output authority for tests and tools; product runtime modules must not depend on it.

prohibitedDependencies.reason: The desktop consumes typed IPC/HTTP contracts and may launch a sidecar; it never imports Python service internals.
Worker invocation crosses the Core API and versioned activity contracts.
Application and domain behavior are presentation-independent.
The Core API cannot depend on presentation libraries.
The Core API cannot depend on visual design contracts.
Workers implement activity contracts and cannot import the application composition root.
Tokens are a lower-level presentation contract.
Reusable components cannot depend on an application composition root.

deploymentProfiles.client: The signed desktop application launches packaged Core API and worker sidecars.
deploymentProfiles.projectAuthority: One local Core API owns the project home, SQLite state, and encrypted object directory.
deploymentProfiles.networkBoundary: Core API binds loopback only and requires an ephemeral capability; offline use remains complete for existing local content.
deploymentProfiles.infrastructureBoundary: No Docker, PostgreSQL, Temporal, Helm, Terraform, tenancy service, or server SSO implementation.

deploymentProfiles.client: The same signed desktop application acts as an authenticated remote-project client with a governed cache and command queue.
deploymentProfiles.projectAuthority: One institution-controlled server project home is authoritative; the desktop never becomes a transparent multi-master.
deploymentProfiles.networkBoundary: OIDC/PKCE, project-scoped authorization, rights-aware egress, TLS, and institutional policy are mandatory.
deploymentProfiles.infrastructureBoundary: Server implementations remain absent until their wave and release gates; current work may define stable portable interfaces only.

deploymentProfiles.client: The same signed desktop application connects to a selected regional project home.
deploymentProfiles.projectAuthority: One regional tenant data plane owns each project; control-plane records remain content-opaque.
deploymentProfiles.networkBoundary: Tenant isolation, residency, metering, policy-aware egress, workload identity, and complete audit are mandatory.
deploymentProfiles.infrastructureBoundary: Multi-tenant control/data planes and elastic infrastructure remain absent until W11 approval.
